entities.summary:
Craterus (b. 369 BCE, Macedonia) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Macedonia. He played a key role in the Hellenistic period, succeeding his father Philotas as leader of the Macedonian army. Craterus's military campaigns expanded Macedonia's territories, contributing to the rise of the Antigonid dynasty.

Craterus was known for his diplomatic efforts, negotiating alliances with neighboring cities and states, including the city-state of Thessaly. He also oversaw the construction of several public buildings, including the city's theater and the palace of the Macedonian royal family.

Craterus's legacy is complex and multifaceted. He was remembered as a skilled military commander and a shrewd politician, who expanded Macedonia's influence and secured its position as a major power in the ancient world. However, his methods were also criticized for their ruthlessness and brutality.

The inscription on Craterus's tombstone, now lost, is said to have been inscribed with the phrase 'Craterus son of Philotas, commander of the Macedonian army', a testament to his status as a prominent leader in the Classical era.

Craterus's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the Hellenistic period, and his contributions to the development of the Antigonid dynasty. His legacy continues to be felt in the ancient world, and his name remains synonymous with bravery, skill, and strategic genius.

Craterus's impact on the ancient world was significant, particularly in the realm of politics and warfare. He was one of the few leaders of his time to have achieved lasting success, and his methods and strategies have been studied by historians and military leaders for centuries.
